Cumulative Frequency of MAPK Pathway Alterations in Post-Hormonal Therapy HR+HER2- Breast Cancers
====================================================================================================

ANSWER: 44.1% (336 of 762 tumors)

Summary
-------
In this MSK-IMPACT genomic profiling cohort from "The Genomic Landscape of Endocrine-Resistant Advanced Breast Cancers" (Razavi et al., 2018, Cancer Cell), the cumulative frequency of MAPK pathway alterations in post-hormonal therapy HR+HER2- tumors is 44.1%.

Cohort Definition
-----------------
- HR+HER2-: RECEPTOR_STATUS_PRIMARY == "HR+/HER2-" (n = 1,422 of 1,918 total)
- Post-hormonal therapy: All non-treatment-naive samples (metastatic sites + post-treatment primaries), n = 762
- Treatment-naive comparison: HR+HER2- primaries with SAMPLE_SITE == "Treatment Naive Primary", n = 660

MAPK Gene Set (29 genes)
------------------------
RTK upstream (14): EGFR, ERBB2, FGFR1, FGFR2, FGFR3, FGFR4, PDGFRA, PDGFRB, KIT, MET, IGF1R, ALK, ROS1, RET
RAS (3): KRAS, NRAS, HRAS
RAF (3): BRAF, RAF1, ARAF
MEK (2): MAP2K1, MAP2K2
ERK (2): MAPK1, MAPK3
Negative regulators (5): NF1, PTPN11, SOS1, RASA1, SPRED1

Alteration Criteria
-------------------
- Activating genes: non-synonymous mutations OR copy-number amplification (CNA >= 1)
- Negative regulators: non-synonymous mutations OR deep deletion (CNA = -2)
- Non-synonymous classes: Missense, Nonsense, Frame_Shift_Del/Ins, Splice_Site, In_Frame_Del/Ins, Translation_Start_Site, Nonstop_Mutation

Key Numbers
-----------
Post-treatment HR+HER2- with ANY MAPK alteration: 336/762 = 44.1%
  - Mutations only: 198/762 = 26.0%
  - CNA only: 138/762 = 18.1%
  - Both: 54/762 = 7.1%

Treatment-naive HR+HER2- comparison: 180/660 = 27.3%
Enrichment test: OR = 2.10, Fisher's exact p = 4.20e-11

Top Individual MAPK Genes
--------------------------
FGFR1: 120/762 = 15.7% (mostly amplification)
ERBB2: 58/762 = 7.6% (mutations + amplification)
NF1:   54/762 = 7.1% (mutations + deep deletion)
IGF1R: 35/762 = 4.6%
FGFR2: 28/762 = 3.7%

Co-occurrence with Established Drivers
--------------------------------------
MAPK vs PIK3CA: OR = 1.25, p = 0.152 (independent, not mutually exclusive)
MAPK vs ESR1:  OR = 0.61, p = 0.023 (significant mutual exclusivity)

Biological Interpretation
-------------------------
MAPK pathway alterations are present in nearly half of post-hormonal therapy HR+HER2- tumors and are significantly enriched compared to treatment-naive primaries (OR = 2.1). The mutual exclusivity with ESR1 mutations (the canonical endocrine-resistance driver at 14.7%) supports MAPK activation as an alternative resistance mechanism -- tumors employ either ESR1 ligand-domain mutations OR MAPK cascade activation, but less commonly both. FGFR1 amplification (15.7%) is the dominant individual event, consistent with published evidence for FGFR signaling as an endocrine-therapy escape route.
